answer: I would like to talk about someone whose talent never stops surprising me. A genuinely talented person I know is a school friend who is an extraordinary musician, particularly on the guitar. We grew up in the same neighbourhood in Sirajganj, and he still plays at local weddings and cultural events. What makes him special is that he seems to play almost [[instinctively]], as though the instrument is an extension of himself. He can pick up a song after hearing it once and play it back perfectly, whether it is an old Bengali folk song or a modern pop hit. I know for a fact, though, that this apparent ease is the result of years of relentless practice. He started as a child on a cheap second-hand guitar and was so [[dedicated]] that he would play for hours until his fingers were sore. He never had formal lessons; he learned by listening to recordings and copying older musicians, sometimes slowing the songs down so he could catch every note. Watching him perform is genuinely [[mesmerising]]; he can shift from a gentle melody to something powerful in seconds. What I respect most is that despite his obvious gift, he remains humble and is always eager to learn from others. I think raw talent only gets you so far, and his discipline is what turned potential into real [[mastery]]. Honestly, seeing someone so devoted to their craft is inspiring, and it reminds me that excellence is rarely accidental.

followUps.q: Have you ever tried to learn the guitar?
followUps.answer: Once, briefly. He gave me a few lessons, but I gave up after about a month because my fingers hurt and I clearly had no [[aptitude]] for it. I am much better at listening.

followUps.q: Do you think he could become a professional musician?
followUps.answer: I think he easily could, if he wanted to. The problem is that music is a risky career here, so he treats it as a passion alongside his regular job, at least for now.

note: Added how I know him, where he plays, his ear for Bengali folk and pop songs and how he taught himself without lessons.
